s50m:S1Q04F.q: How would you reduce the sorting cost for millions of customers while preserving the tie rule?
s50m:S1Q04F.label: gemini-3.1-flash-lite_fturn-s50m-A
s50m:S1Q04F.spoken: I’d use a min-heap of size K to maintain the top candidates, which reduces the complexity to O(N log K). To handle the tie rule, I’d define a composite key—the score and a secondary identifier like the user ID—so the comparison remains deterministic. If N is massive, I’d use Quickselect for O(N) average time complexity.

s50m:S1Q06F.q: How would you index those tables, and what changes if historical records can be corrected after ingestion?
s50m:S1Q06F.label: gemini-3.1-flash-lite_fturn-s50m-A
s50m:S1Q06F.spoken: I'd index the join keys, specifically customer_id. For time-series lookups, I'd use a composite index on (customer_id, event_timestamp). If records change after ingestion, I’d move to an updated_at column and a versioning or SCD Type 2 pattern. This ensures we maintain an accurate audit trail and don't invalidate historical snapshots when corrections occur.

s50m:S2Q05F.q: Construct an example where that greedy policy gives poor coverage, and tell me how you would incorporate redundancy or multi hop dependence
s50m:S2Q05F.label: gemini-3.1-flash-lite_fturn-s50m-A
s50m:S2Q05F.spoken: A greedy policy fails when the top results are semantically redundant. For example, if I ask about "Drug X side effects," and the top three documents all describe the same headache symptom, I get zero coverage of other side effects. To fix this, I use Maximal Marginal Relevance, or MMR, which balances relevance with novelty by penalizing chunks that are too similar to what's already selected. The key dependency is the embedding model's ability to distinguish subtle semantic differences; if the embeddings are too coarse, MMR can't effectively filter redundancy. I also have to carefully tune the lambda parameter to balance the trade-off between strict relevance and diversity.

s50m:S2Q08F.q: How do you prove the replacement index is sufficiently complete and current before you send production traffic to it?
s50m:S2Q08F.label: gemini-3.1-flash-lite_fturn-s50m-A
s50m:S2Q08F.spoken: I run the new index in a shadow environment, processing a subset of live traffic alongside the production index. I compare retrieval quality against a golden dataset using an LLM-as-judge pipeline to verify coverage and accuracy. I also run a data-freshness check to ensure the ingestion pipeline has fully synchronized all documents before I trigger the cutover.
